title: Finite graded modules flat over a local coefficient ring are finitely presented
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a nonzero commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal. Let $n\geq0$ and let $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ be positive integers. Give $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] the grading in which $R$ has degree $0$ and $x_i$ has degree $w_i$: $P_d$ is the $R$-span of monomials $x^\alpha$ with $\sum_iw_i\alpha_i=d$ (and $P_d=0$ for $d<0$). Let $L$ be a $P$-module with an internal grading $L=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbf Z}L_d$ by $R$-submodules satisfying $P_eL_d\subseteq L_{e+d}$. If $L$ is finite as a $P$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $L$ is finitely presented as a $P$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Tag 053C, lemma-flat-graded-finite-type-finite-presentation-module, statement at lines 5856--5870 and proof at lines 5873--5909

proof.text: Replace a finite generating family by its finitely many homogeneous components; their span contains the original generators, so they still generate. Choose these homogeneous generators $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ of $L$ over $P$ (finite generation). With $d_i=\deg(m_i)$, they give a graded exact sequence $0\to K\to\bigoplus_i P(-d_i)\to L\to0$, whose degree-$d$ part is $0\to K_d\to\bigoplus_i P_{d-d_i}\to L_d\to0$. For each $d$, the module $P_{d-d_i}$ is finite free over $R$: only finitely many exponent vectors $\alpha$ satisfy $\sum_j w_j\alpha_j=d-d_i$, because all $w_j>0$; its monomials form a finite basis. The inclusion and degree projection exhibit $L_d$ as an $R$-linear retract of $L$, so $L_d$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-retract]. The middle term is finite free and hence flat (tensoring with it is a finite direct sum, which preserves injections). Thus each $K_d$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ses-kernel-flat].

Each $L_d$ is a finite flat $R$-module: it is generated over $R$ by the finitely many products of the chosen $m_i$ with monomials of degree $d-d_i$, and it is a direct graded summand of the flat $R$-module $L$, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-retract]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] makes every $L_d$ finite free. The surjection $\bigoplus_i P_{d-d_i}\to L_d$ then splits because $L_d$ is free, so $K_d$ is a retract of the finite free source and is finite. Together with Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free], each $K_d$ is finite free.

Let $\mathfrak m$ be the unique maximal ideal of $R$ and $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$. Since each $L_d$ is flat over $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] shows that tensoring the degreewise exact sequences with $\kappa$ preserves exactness. The ring $P\otimes_R\kappa\cong\kappa[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (the base $\kappa$ is a field, hence Noetherian), and the injected module $K\otimes_R\kappa$ is a submodule of the finite $P\otimes_R\kappa$-module $\bigoplus_i(P\otimes_R\kappa)(-d_i)$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] makes $K\otimes_R\kappa$ finite over $P\otimes_R\kappa$, and homogeneous finite generators $\bar k_1,\ldots,\bar k_t$ may be chosen. Choose homogeneous lifts $k_j\in K$ and write $e_j=\deg(k_j)$.

For every degree $d$, the homogeneous map $\bigoplus_j P_{d-e_j}\to K_d$ induced by the $k_j$ becomes surjective after tensoring with $\kappa$, because the $\bar k_j$ generate $K\otimes_R\kappa$ homogeneously. Its cokernel is a finite $R$-module: both source and target are finite $R$-modules by Step 2. Nakayama's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] therefore makes this map surjective over $R$. Hence the finite set $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ generates $K$ as a graded $P$-module. Thus $K$ is finitely generated, and the exact sequence in Step 1 is a finite presentation of $L$ over $P$ by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].
